article.hook: You hesitate to call your view ‘right’ - but you replay it anyway. Chiron in Sagittarius catches us wrestling with whether our perspective matters at all. This isn’t a quick fix; it’s years of learning to trust your own map in a world full of louder claims.
article.lived: Chiron spends years in Sagittarius, stretching the slow arc of doubt around belief. You notice it when you pause before sharing an opinion, hearing your own voice soften or shrink. We all live through moments when the urge to stand firm crashes into the fear that what we see might be wrong or worth less. That hesitation colors conversations, decisions, even small choices like what book to read or what causes to support.
article.turn: This wound flips when insecurity becomes silence or stubbornness - shutting down to avoid being ‘wrong,’ or doubling down to block out challenge. Neither defends your view; both erase it. The only way out is showing up with your truth, even if it trembles and feels unsteady. There is no safety in silence when your perspective is what needs to be known.
moves: Read one article or book that challenges your beliefs and summarize your take in a message to someone.
Speak your opinion aloud at least once in a conversation where you usually stay quiet.
Write down the exact reasons you doubt your view, then rewrite each as a question to explore, not a conclusion.
